name: arid1b-related disorder
definition: Disease caused by mutation or copy number variation in ARID1B.

name: spinocerebellar ataxia 51
definition: Spinocerebellar ataxia-51 (SCA51) is an autosomal dominant neurologic disorder characterized by progressive gait abnormalities, ataxia, and dysarthria.

name: ebv-positive nodal t- and nk-cell lymphoma
definition: An EBV-positive T-cell/NK-cell lymphoma that arises from the lymph nodes. It is characterized by a monomorphic pattern of infiltration and abscence of the angiodestruction and necrosis seen in extranodal NK/T-cell lymphomas. These lymphomas are more common in elderly patient, or in the setting of immune deficiency.

name: hereditary cancer
definition: Malignant neoplasms occurring in families at a rate greater than that expected by chance and caused by germline mutations in a specific gene.

name: ano5-related muscle diseases
definition: Anoctaminopathy-5 refers to a group of hereditary skeletal muscle or bone disorders due to mutations in the anoctamin 5 (ANO5)-encoding gene

name: channelopathy
definition: Channelopathies are a group of diseases caused by the dysfunction of ion channel subunits or their interacting proteins.

name: preserved ratio impaired spirometry
definition: It is defined as forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) <80% predicted and FEV1/forced vital capacity (FVC) ratio ≥0.70.

name: early infantile epileptic encephalopathy, autosomal recessive
tryptophan 5-monooxygenase deficiency
definition: Tryptophan 5-monooxygenase deficiency is a rare genetic disorder that can lead to a number of health conditions.

name: social risk factor
definition: Social factors such as personal behavior, lifestyle, or environment belonging to the subject which are known to increase the likelihood of infection and disease.

name: colorectal neuroendocrine tumor
definition: A well differentiated, low, intermediate, or high grade neoplasm with neuroendocrine differentiation that arises from the colon or rectum.

name: melanoma in situ of ear and external auricular canal
definition: Evidence of melanoma in situ of ear and external auricular canal.

name: benign orbit neoplasm
definition: A neoplasm that arises from the orbit and is characterized by the absence of atypical or malignant cytological and architectural features, and absence of invasive features or metastatic potential.

name: mastoidectomy
definition: Total or partial excision of the mastoid process.

name: coronary revascularization procedure
definition: Any procedure that is undertaken to reestablish blood flow to the heart.

name: cholecystectomy
definition: Surgical removal of the gallbladder.

name: oral cavity cyst
definition: A cystic lesion located in the oral cavity.

name: lichenoid drug reaction
definition: A red or violaceous flat-topped, papular eruption that is induced by exposure to a variety of medications or environmental agents.

name: spinal fusion
definition: Fusing two or more vertebrae into one.

name: infective spondylopathy
definition: Evidence of other infective spondylopathies, site unspecified not specified elsewhere.

name: low grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia
definition: Squamous or glandular cervical intraepithelial neoplasia characterized by the presence of mild dysplastic changes.

name: high grade vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia
definition: Vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia characterized by the presence of moderate or severe dysplastic changes.

name: low grade vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia
definition: Vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia characterized by the presence of koilocytosis and disorganization and thickening of the basal layer.

name: high grade vulvar squamous intraepithelial lesion
definition: An intraepithelial lesion of the vulvar squamous epithelium associated with HPV infection. It is characterized by loss of maturation, nuclear hyperchromasia, high nuclear:cytoplasmic ratios, cytological and architectural atypia, and mitoses. Two morphological patterns have been described: basaloid (undifferentiated) and warty (condylomatous, bowenoid). It carries a significant but relatively low risk of progression to squamous cell carcinoma if untreated. (WHO 2020)

name: low grave vulvar squamous intraepithelial lesion
definition: An intraepithelial lesion of the vulvar squamous epithelium associated with HPV infection. It is characterized by mild cytologic atypia.

name: labor and delivery complications
definition: The occurrence of a pregnancy complication during childbirth, which includes both labor (the process of childbirth) and delivery (the birth itself).

name: neonatal injury related to birth
definition: An injury sustained to a neonate during the birthing process.

name: congenital respiratory system disorder
definition: An abnormality of the respiratory system that is present at birth or detected in the neonatal period.

name: immunohistochemistry
definition: A method using antibodies to detect specific antigens, to determine presence/absence of a protein or a portion of a protein e.g. the C-terminus.

name: immunofluorescence assay
definition: A method using fluorescently labelled antibodies to detect the presence and/or localization of a protein or other molecule within cells or tissues.

name: Western blotting
definition: A method using separation of proteins by gel electrophoresis and antibodies to detect the presence and/or quantity of a protein or other molecule

name: in vitro motility assay
definition: A method to evaluate the interaction of myosin and actin as a measure of the movement of motor proteins in muscle

name: enzyme assay
definition: A method to measure enzymatic activity.

name: patch clamp
definition: An electrophysiological method to measure ion currents in individual cells.

name: subcellular protein localization assay
definition: A method to determine where a protein localizes within cells.

name: promoter activity assay
definition: A method using a reporter gene to measue the activity of a gene's promoter.

name: DNA binding assay
definition: A method to measure the interaction of proteins with DNA, e.g. for transcription or DNA repair.

name: cell survival assay
definition: A method used to measure survival of cells following introduction of a genetic variant.

name: animal model
definition: An animal used to model the effects of a genetic variant on the organism as a whole.

name: chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
definition: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) is characterized by the persistence of thromboemboli in the form of organized tissue obstructing the pulmonary arteries. The consequence is an increase in pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) resulting in pulmonary hypertension (PH) and progressive right heart failure.

name: imaging based spatial transcriptomics
definition: An assay for in situ identification of mRNA molecules within tissues via microscopy.

name: Vizgen MERSCOPE
definition: Merscope is a high-resolution, in situ spatial imaging platform that combines single-cell and spatial multiomics analyses in one integrated system.

name: early-onset Alzheimers disease
definition: A rare form of Alzheimer's disease, occurring before the age of 65.

name: income
definition: A gain or recurrent benefit during a period of time, usually measured in money that derives from capital or labor.

name: hand eczema
definition: A form of contact dermatitis characterised by inflammation, redness and itching of the hands.

name: female chronic pelvic pain
definition: Chronic pelvis pain in women.

name: GATA1 gene mutation
definition: A mutation in the chromosome X gene, GATA1.

name: STARmap
definition: STARmap is an image-based technology for 3D intact-tissue RNA sequencing, which integrates hydrogel-tissue chemistry, targeted signal amplification, and in situ sequencing.

name: sci-CAR
synonyms: single-cell combinatorial indexing chromatin accessibility and mRNA profiling
definition: A combinatorial indexing-based coassay that jointly profiles chromatin accessibility and mRNA (CAR) in each of thousands of single cells, combining sci–ATAC sequencing (sci-ATAC-seq) and sci-RNA-seq into a single protocol.

name: microwell-seq
definition: A platform for high-throughput single-cell RNA-sequencing. An agarose plate with microwells is used to trap 5-10K individual cells. Barcoded magnetic beads are loaded and trapped into each well. Each single bead is conjugated with 107–108 oligonucleotides, which share the same cellular barcode. Each oligonucleotide consists of a primer sequence, a cell barcode, a unique molecular identifier (UMI), and a poly T tail. After incubation of beads and cells in a soft flow of lysis buffer, beads with captured mRNA are retrieved with a magnet. Beads are collected in a tube in which reverse transcription and template switch steps are performed using the Smart-seq2 protocol (Picelli et al., 2013). Amplified cDNA is fragmented by a customized transposase that carries two identical insertion sequences. The 3′ ends of the transcripts are then enriched during library generation using PCR and sequenced using an Illumina Sequencing Platform.

name: 10x 3' transcription profiling
definition: 10x 3' transcription profiling is the 10x-based single-cell technology that sequences mRNA molecules from their 3' end.

name: 10x 5' transcription profiling
definition: 10x 5' transcription profiling is the 10x-based single-cell technology that sequences mRNA molecules from their 5' end.

name: spatial transcriptomics by high-throughput sequencing
definition: A spatial transcriptomics assay that measures spatially defined transcription by high-throughput sequencing.

name: immune sequencing
definition: A sequencing assays that collects a multitude of genetic sequences for B Cell Receptors (BCRs) and T Cell Receptors (TCRs) within a tissue (these loci show large amounts of somatic mutations).

name: 10x scATAC-seq
definition: A single cell ATAC-seq method for profiling of chromatin accessibility. For library construction, single cells or single nuclei are isolated into droplets using 10x Chromium technnolgy.

name: CITE-seq (cell surface protein profiling)
definition: The use of CITE-seq technology with the purpose of quantifying cell surface protein expression in addition to transcriptomic readout in single cells.

name: CITE-seq (sample multiplexing)
definition: The use of CITE-seq technology with the purpose of multiplexing single-cell samples from different sources.

name: 10x feature profiling
definition: 10x feature barcode technology is a method for adding extra channels of information to cells by running single-cell gene expression in parallel with other assays. This is done by generating additional sequencing libraries within the same droplet containing a single cell. The readout of these libraries are known oligonucleotides that are coupled to cell surface proteins antibodies or sgRNAs.

name: 10x feature barcode (cell surface protein profiling)
definition: The use of 10x Genomics feature barcode technology with the purpose of quantifying cell surface protein expression in addition to transcriptomic readout in single cells.

name: 10x feature barcode (sample multiplexing)
definition: The use of 10x Genomics feature barcode technology with the purpose of multiplexing single-cell samples from different sources.

name: 10x feature barcode (CRISPR screening)
definition: The use of 10x Genomics feature barcode technology with the purpose of performing a CRISPR screening.

name: bulk immune repertoire sequencing
definition: An immune repertoire sequencing assay that lyses cells and sequences BCRs and TCRs indiscriminately.

name: single cell immune repertoire sequencing
definition: An immune repertoire sequencing assay that sequences BCRs and TCRs that can be mapped to a single cell.

name: sample splitting
definition: Physical separation of a material, e.g. tissue obtained from a biopsy, into discrete instances.

name: BLaER1
definition: BLaER1 cell line is a tamoxifen-inducible subclone of the RCH-ACV B-cell leukemia cell line genetically modified using a retrovirus vector to express C/EBPα fused with the estrogen receptor hormone binding domain (ER) and GFP.

name: Seq-Well S3
definition: Seq-Well with second strand synthesis.

name: breast milk collection
definition: Collection of a breast milk specimen from an organism.

name: Nx1-seq
definition: Next generation one-cell sequencing (Nx1-seq) is a single cell transcriptomic library preparation method which conjugates polystyrene beads to barcode nucleotides by means of emulsion PCR using oligo-dTs. The beads are mixed on a chamber slide containing PDMS microwells which fit one cell per well. The slide is then washed with a cell suspension to capture and barcode individual cells.

name: raw matrix generation
definition: A data transformation process involved in generating a raw matrix from raw data.

name: processed matrix generation
definition: A data transformation process involved in generating a processed matrix from sequence data and/or count matrices, including demultiplexing samples, quality control, normalization, data correction, and feature selection.

name: analysis of matrices
definition: A data transformation process involved in analysing expression matrices, including visualisation, comparison or integration with other datasets, clustering, and differential expression analysis.

name: spatial analysis
definition: A data transformation process involved in analysing spatial images or data.

name: sci-Plex
definition: The combination of nuclear hashing and sci-RNA-seq into a single workflow for multiplex transcriptomics, enabling the capture of gene expression profiles from thousands of experimental conditions in a single experiment.

name: snmC-Seq2
definition: A protocol for single nucleus methylcytosine sequencing. snmC-seq2 provides improved read mapping, reduced artifactual reads, enhanced throughput, as well as increased library complexity and coverage uniformity compared to snmC-seq.

name: sci-RNA-seq3
definition: Single-cell combinatorial indexing (‘sci-’) is a methodological framework that employs split-pool barcoding to uniquely label the nucleic acid contents of large numbers of single cells or nuclei. The sci-RNA-seq3 is an updated version of sci-RNA-seq. The major improvements are: (1) nuclei are extracted directly from fresh tissues without enzymatic treatment; (2) hairpin ligation for the third level indexing (barcoded Tn5 tagmentation was used in the previous version); (3) individually optimised enzymatic reactions; (4) FACS was replaced by dilution, and sonication and filtration steps were added to minimize aggregation.

name: NanoString digital spatial profiling
definition: A spatial transcriptomics by high-throughput sequencing assay which enables spatial analysis of RNA and protein in tissue specimens on slides.

name: Quant-seq
definition: QuantSeq provides an easy protocol to generate highly strand-specific next-generation sequencing (NGS) libraries close to the 3′ end of polyadenylated RNAs within 4.5 h.

name: SCOPE-chip
definition: The SCOPE-chip captures single cells by partitioning them into hundreds of thousands of microwells on the chip following the Poisson distribution. Afterwards, an excess of Barcoding Beads is added to the microwells of the chip; the diameter of the beads versus that of the microwells ensuring that only one Barcoding Bead falls into each microwell. After cell lysis, Barcoding Beads, each with a unique cell label (Barcode), capture mRNA by binding to the poly (A) tail. Barcoding Beads are subsequently collected from the microwell chip, followed by reverse transcription of the mRNA captured by the Barcoding Beads into cDNA, and subsequent PCR amplification. The amplified cDNA is then fragmented and ligated with sequencing adapters. The end result is an NGS library that is compatible with Illumina sequencing instruments, that can also be run on Pacbio and MGI sequencing platforms with minor modifications.

name: B6.SJL-Slc6a3tm1.1(cre)Bkmn/J
definition: DATIREScre knock-in mice have Cre recombinase expression directed to dopaminergic neurons, without disrupting endogenous dopamine transporter expression. These mice may be useful for studying gene function in dopaminergic neurons, such as drug addiction, Parkinson's disease and Attention Deficit-Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD).

name: gRNA-seq
synonyms: Amplicon sequencing of gRNAs from CRISPR pooled genetic screens. gRNAs are integrated into the cell genome, so sequencing is done on genomic DNA.

name: shRNA-seq
definition: Amplicon sequencing of shRNAs from RNAi pooled genetic screens. shRNA constructs are integrated into the cell genome, so sequencing is done on genomic DNA.

name: cancer cell line sample
definition: A neoplastic sample derived from a cancer cell line.

name: bronchoscopic microsampling
definition: A biopsy in which a device consisting of a wire with a polyester probe at the tip is used to collect bronchial epithelial lining fluid with bronchoscopy.

name: T cell activation assay
definition: An assay in which T cells are incubated with a culture media containing an activator agent (such as Dynabeads Human T-Activator CD3/CD28), mimicking the natural activation and expansion process.

name: follow-up status
definition: The status of a follow-up procedure. It is a common observation in e.g. clinical treatment trials.

name: no follow-up status
definition: The absence of information on a follow-up status.

name: recorded follow-up status
definition: The presence of information on a follow-up status.

name: alive (follow-up status)
definition: A recorded follow-up status noting that a patient is alive.

name: alive with disease
definition: A recorded follow-up status noting that a patient is alive and still has the disease under study.

name: alive in partial remission
definition: A recorded follow-up status noting that a patient is alive and that the disease is in partial remission.

name: alive with stable disease
definition: A recorded follow-up status noting that a patient is alive and that the disease is stable.

name: alive with recurrent disease
definition: A recorded follow-up status noting that a patient is alive and that the disease is recurrent.

name: alive with progressive disease
definition: A recorded follow-up status noting that a patient is alive and that the disease is progressive.

name: alive with metastatic disease
definition: A recorded follow-up status noting that a patient is alive and that the disease is metastatic.

name: alive in complete remission
definition: A recorded follow-up status noting that a patient is alive and in complete remission from the condition under study.

name: dead (follow-up status)
definition: A recorded follow-up status noting that a patient died.

name: death from disease
definition: A recorded follow-up status noting that a patient died from the same condition under study.

name: death from other causes
definition: A recorded follow-up status noting that a patient died from other causes than the condition under study.

name: nuclear RNA
definition: An RNA extract that is the output of an extraction process in which RNA molecules found in the nucleus, including mRNA precursors (pre-mRNA), are extracted.

name: pseudo-bulk aggregation of single-cell expression data
definition: A processed matrix generation method that involves combining single-cell expression values from multiple cells in the same biological sample. Aggregation is typically performed by summation of count data for cells of the same (inferred) type. The aggregated expression profiles can then be used in the same manner as bulk RNA-seq data, especially in differential expression analyses.

name: label-free quantification
definition: A proteomic profiling method that uses mass spectrometry to quantify the relative amount of each protein across multiple biological samples without the need for any prior sample labelling. The assay is run separately on each sample and involves digestion of the proteome into peptides, liquid chromatography with mass spectrometry, and then quantification via spectral counting (i.e., the number of matching spectra from MS/MS) or integration of the intensities of each peptide's peaks.

name: 16S metagenomic sequencing
definition: An amplicon sequencing approach targeting the variable regions of the 16S ribosomal RNA gene. This is commonly used to quantify the abundance of different microbial taxa in an environmental sample, based on how frequently a taxa's specific rRNA sequence is observed in the sequencing data.

name: tandem mass spectrometry
definition: A mass spectrometry assay that combines two mass spectrometers together to analyze complex biomolecules such as peptides. The first instrument separates ionized molecules by their mass-to-charge ratio and filters for ions at a particular ratio. Once isolated, these ions are fragmented into smaller ions that are analyzed with the second instrument. The mass-charge filter and fragment spectra are then compared to a reference database to identify the original molecule.

name: Luminex multi-analyte profiling
definition: The Luminex technology is a bead-based assay for quantification of multiple analytes in a single sample. Beads are color-coded and coated with antibodies or oligonucleotide primers specific to different analytes. After incubation with the sample of interest, secondary antibodies/primers are added, and imaging of the beads can be used to quantify the abundance of each analyte.

name: transcription profiling by NanoString
definition: The NanoString nCounter gene expression system uses multiplexed probe hybridization to capture and count individual mRNA transcripts. Transcripts for each gene are targeted by a pair of gene-specific probes - a biotinylated capture probe to capture the transcript on a streptavidin-coated slide, and a reporter probe containing a color-coded pattern of fluorescent segments. Imaging of the slide can then identify each captured transcript.

name: 10x multiome
synonyms: Chromium Single Cell Multiome ATAC + Gene Expression
definition: Simultaneous profiling of gene expression and open chromatin from the same cell.

name: mCT-seq
definition: A method that can jointly capture cytosine DNA methylome (5mC) and transcriptome profiles from single cells/nuclei by partitioning RNA and DNA molecules through the incorporation of 5’-methyl-dCTP instead of dCTP during reverse transcription of RNA.

name: mcSCRB-seq
synonyms: molecular crowding single-cell RNA barcoding and sequencing
definition: A single-cell RNA barcoding and sequencing protocol with increased sensitivity through the addition of polyethylene glycol (PEG 8000). PEG 8000 increases the cDNA yield by reducing the effective reaction volume.

name: Slide-seqV2
definition: More sensitive version of the Slide-seq method for transferring RNA from tissue sections onto a surface covered in DNA-barcoded beads with known positions, which differs from Slide-seq in the use of a monobase encoding scheme with sequencing by ligation using sequential interrogation by offset primer, and improved parameters for split-pool synthesis of barcoded beads.

name: copy number assessment
definition: Result of genomic copy number assessment of a genomic element or region.

name: regional base ploidy
definition: Copy number assessment of regional base ploidy.

name: copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity
definition: Assessment of copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity.

name: relative copy number variation
definition: Assessment of relative copy number variation.

name: copy number loss
definition: Assessment of genomic copy number loss.

name: low-level copy number loss
definition: Assessment of low-level genomic copy number loss.

name: complete genomic deletion
definition: Assessment of complete genomic deletion.

name: copy number gain
definition: Assessment of genomic copy number gain.

name: low-level copy number gain
definition: Assessment of low-level genomic copy number gain.

name: high-level copy number gain
definition: Assessment of high-level genomic copy number gain.

name: focal genome amplification
definition: Assessment of focal genome amplification.

name: SORT-seq
definition: A partially robotized version of the CEL-seq2 protocol that uses FACS to sort single cells into the wells of a 384-well cell-capture plate. Each well in the plate contains barcoded primers and other reagents. This sorting step makes it possible to analyze live single cells, or any other particular population of interest.

name: cDNA microarray
definition: A DNA array that contains probes (usually many thousands of them) generated from the reverse transcription of messenger RNA and propagated in bacterial vectors. While the main application of cDNA microarrays is in the generation of transcriptomic profiles, they also can be used for genomic analyses such as copy number profiling experiments.

name: methylation-specific microarray
definition: An oligonucleotide DNA microarray that employs specifically designed oligonucleotides to probe the methylation status of e.g. CpG and CpHpG sites. It may also be applied to derive additional information such as genomic copy number variations.

name: cell hashing
definition: A single cell library construction process that involves labelling cells with sample-specific oligonucleotides, typically through antibody- or lipid-based reagents, such that cells from distinct samples can be pooled together for single-cell sequencing. This multiplexed approach increases throughput, eliminates batch effects, and enables detection of multiplets.

name: droplet-based single-cell RNA library preparation
definition: A single-cell RNA library construction method that is droplet-based.

name: paracentesis
definition: A specimen-collecting procedure in which a needle or catheter is inserted into the peritoneal cavity to obtain ascitic fluid for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes. Ascitic fluid may be used to help determine the etiology of ascites, as well as to evaluate for infection or presence of cancer.

name: 10x transcription profiling
definition: The 10x-based single-cell technology that sequences mRNA molecules.

name: HLA typing by NGS
synonyms: HLA typing using Next Generation Sequencing
definition: A method for identification of HLA antigen polymorphisms using a high-throughput sequencing platform.

name: polygenic risk score
definition: An estimate of an individual’s genetic risk for some traits, obtained by aggregating and quantifying the effect of many common variants in the genome (usually defined as minor allele frequency ≥1%), each of which can have a small effect on a person’s genetic risk for a given disease or condition.

name: clinical data
definition: A data set containing clinical information.

name: sortilin measurement
definition: Quantification of the amount of sortilin in a sample.

name: ghrelin measurement
definition: Quantification of the amount of ghrelin present in a sample.

name: obsolete_retinal layer thickness measurement
definition: A measure of the thickness of one or more layers of the retina. It is measured with various imaging tools including ultrasound, optical coherence tomography (OCT), confocal microscopy, and biometry. Reduced retinal layer thickness is one of the biomarkers used for the diagnosis of glaucoma.

name: vitamin C measurement
definition: Quantification of vitamin C levels in a sample.

name: obsolete_retinal nerve fibre layer thickness measurement
synonyms: peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer thickness measurement
definition: A measure of the thickness of the retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL). It is typically measured using optical imaging methods such as optical coherence tomography (OCT). The thickness of the ganglion cell complex (GCC), the collective name for the retinal nerve fibre layer and the ganglion cell inner plexiform layer, is one of the biomarkers used in the diagnosis of primary open angle glaucoma (POAG).

name: obsolete_ganglion cell inner plexiform layer thickness measurement
definition: A measure of the thickness of the ganglion cell inner plexiform layer (GCIPL). It is typically measured using optical imaging methods such as optical coherence tomography (OCT). The thickness of the ganglion cell complex (GCC), the collective name for the retinal nerve fibre layer and the ganglion cell inner plexiform layer, is one of the biomarkers used in the diagnosis of primary open angle glaucoma (POAG).

name: human herpesvirus 7 seropositivity
definition: human herpesvirus 7 seropositivity is the result of a measurement of circulating human herpesvirus 7 specific antibodies

name: fish oil supplement exposure measurement
definition: Quantification of some aspect of an individual's exposure to fish oil supplementation.

name: mitochondrial heteroplasmy measurement
definition: A quantification of the degree of mitochondrial heteroplasmy, i.e. the presence of different mitochondrial DNA variants in different mitochondria within the same individual organism or cell. Heteroplasmy can be inherited through the maternal germ line, or arise through somatic mitochondrial mutations within an individual.

name: cardiac ablation
definition: Cardiac or catheter ablation is a minimally invasive procedure used to remove or terminate a faulty electrical pathway from sections of the hearts of those who are prone to developing cardiac arrhythmias such as atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, SVT and Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.

name: emodin glucuronidation measurement
definition: Quantification of emodin metabolisation via the glucuronidation pathway.

name: Parkinson's disease symptom measurement
definition: Quantification of some aspect of Parkinson's disease symptoms such as their frequency, severity or ratio.

name: S100 calcium-binding protein B measurement
definition: The quantification of S100 calcium-binding protein B in a sample.

name: response to ropeginterferon alfa-2b
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of any ropeginterferon alfa-2b stimulus. Ropeginterferon alfa-2b is a medication used to treat polycythemia vera.

name: ropeginterferon alfa-2b
definition: A long-acting formulation of recombinant interferon alpha subtype 2b (IFN-a2b), in which IFN-a2b is coupled, via proline, to polyethylene glycol (PEG), with antiviral, immunomodulating and antineoplastic activities. Upon administration of ropeginterferon alfa-2b, IFN-a2b targets and binds to specific IFN cell-surface receptors. This activates IFN-mediated signal transduction pathways and induces the transcription and translation of genes with IFN-specific response elements (ISREs). Their protein products mediate antiviral, antiproliferative, anticancer, and immune-modulating effects. The PEG moiety inhibits proteolytic breakdown and clearance of IFN-a2b, which prolongs its half-life, extends the duration of its therapeutic effects and allows less frequent dosing. The proline linker facilitates the synthesis of a single positional isomer which further increases its stability and half-life.

name: noise exposure measurement
definition: Quantification of some aspect of noise exposure, such as occupational levels.

name: plasma beta-amyloid 1-40:1-42 ratio measurement
definition: Quantification of the ratio of beta-amyloid 1-40 to 1-42 proteins in a sample of blood plasma.

name: obsolete_response to dolutegravir
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) in response to the anti-retroviral drug dolutegravir, typically used in the treatment of HIV infection.

name: trabecular bone score
definition: The trabecular bone score (TBS) is an analytical tool used to measure grey-level textures on lumbar spine (LS) dual X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) images. It is a measure of bone texture correlated with bone microarchitecture and is associated with the incidence of new fracture.

name: COVID-19 symptoms measurement
definition: Quantification of some aspect of COVID-19 symptoms, such as severity or time to remission.

name: time to remission of COVID-19 symptoms
definition: Quantification of time to remission of COVID-19 symptoms.

name: response to dietary selenium supplementation
definition: Physiological response of an organism to being given selenium as a dietary supplement.

name: response to gamma-aminobutyric acid receptor agonists
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a gamma-aminobutyric acid receptor agonist.

name: response to immune checkpoint inhibitor
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of immune checkpoint inhibitor stimulus such as Ipilimumab and Anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agents.

name: obsolete_response to tofacitinib
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus with tofacitinib.

name: obsolete_aortic vascular smooth muscle cell calcification measurement
definition: Quantification of the calcification of vascular smooth muscle cells derived from the aorta.

name: obsolete_aortic vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation measurement
definition: Quantification of the multiplication or reproduction of vascular smooth muscle cells derived from the aorta.

name: hemoglobin change measurement
definition: Quantification of the change in hemoglobin levels in an individual over time, eg over the course of several years after regular blood donation.

name: N-acylethanolamine measurement
definition: Quantification of the levels of N-acylethanolamine in a sample.

name: response to antiparasitic agent
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an antiparasitic agent.

name: response to benznidazole
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of benznidazole (BZN) stimulus. BZN is the main drug with activity against Trypanosoma cruzi, a parasite that causes Chagas disease also referred to as American trypanosomiasis.

name: congenital right-sided heart lesions
definition: Serious heritable structural anomalies of the right side of the heart, including pulmonary atresia, tricuspid valve disease and Ebstein's anomaly, and right ventricular outflow tract obstruction and/or pulmonary stenosis, that are present from birth.

name: response to mitochondrial complex I inhibitor
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a mitochondrial complex I inhibitor (MCI) stimulus. MCI is a small molecule druggable target with downstream signalling that engages multiple neuroprotective mechanisms alleviating cognitive decline and neurodegeneration.

name: response to neuromuscular blocker
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a neuromuscular blocker.

name: obsolete_heart left atrium capacity
definition: Quantification of the volume of or amount contained in the left upper chamber of the heart.

name: obsolete_muscle fiber cross-sectional area measurement
definition: Quantification of a muscle fiber cross-sectional area by muscle biopsy. It is a microscopic measure of muscle fiber size and structure to assess skeletal muscle hypertrophy typically in the context of resistance training.

name: resistance training
definition: Physical exercise that uses weight, or other forms of resistance, to induce muscle contraction and build strength, anaerobic endurance, and size of skeletal muscles. Typical exercises include leg and chest press, knee extension, leg curl, row, abdominal crunch, and bicep curl.

name: plasma clozapine measurement
definition: Quantification of the levels of clozapine in blood plasma. Clozapine is an antipsychotic drug used to treat schizophrenia.

name: plasma N-desmethylclozapine measurement
definition: Quantification of the levels of N-desmethylclozapine, also known as norclozapine, in blood plasma. N-desmethylclozapine is a major active metabolite of clozapine, an antipsychotic drug used to treat schizophrenia.

name: plasma clozapine-to-N-desmethylclozapine ratio measurement
definition: Quantification of the ratio of clozapine to-N-desmethylclozapine, also known as norclozapine, in blood plasma. Clozapine is an antipsychotic drug used to treat schizophrenia and N-desmethylclozapine is a a major active metabolite of clozapine.

name: obsolete_serum clozapine measurement
definition: Quantification of the levels of clozapine in blood serum. Clozapine is an antipsychotic drug used to treat schizophrenia.

name: serum clozapine-to-N-desmethylclozapine ratio measurement
definition: Quantification of the ratio of clozapine to-N-desmethylclozapine, also known as norclozapine, in blood serum. Clozapine is an antipsychotic drug used to treat schizophrenia and N-desmethylclozapine is a a major active metabolite of clozapine.

name: obsolete_serum N-desmethylclozapine measurement
definition: Quantification of the levels of N-desmethylclozapine, also known as norclozapine, in blood serum. N-desmethylclozapine is a a major active metabolite of clozapine, an antipsychotic drug used to treat schizophrenia.

name: obsolete_kidney volume
definition: Quantification of the volume of the kidney.

name: obsolete_pancreas volume
definition: Quantification of the volume of the pancreas.

name: obsolete_lung volume
definition: Quantification of the volume of the lung.

name: obsolete_spleen volume
definition: Quantification of the volume of the spleen.

name: obsolete_liver volume
definition: Quantification of the volume of the liver.

name: obsolete_pancreas fat measurement
definition: Quantification of the fat content of the pancreas.

name: plasma leucine rich alpha-2-glycoprotein 1 measurement
definition: Quantification of the levels of leucine rich alpha-2-glycoprotein 1 present in a sample.

name: response to smoking cessation agent
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a smoking cessation agent. These include nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) agents that are available as nicotine patches, gums, lozenges or inhalers and nicotinic receptor antagonists such as varenicline and buproprion.

name: response to varenicline
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of varenicline, a nicotinic acetylcholine receptor agonist used as a smoking cessation agent. Varenicline is also used for the treatment of dry eye disease.

name: complement factor H-related proteins measurement
definition: Quantification of the amount of complement factor H-related proteins in a sample.

name: complement factor H-related protein 1 measurement
definition: Quantification of the amount of complement factor H-related protein 1 in a sample.

name: complement factor H-related protein 2 measurement
definition: Quantification of the amount of complement factor H-related protein 2 in a sample.

name: complement factor H-related protein 3 measurement
definition: Quantification of the amount of complement factor H-related protein 3 in a sample.

name: complement factor H-related protein 4A measurement
definition: Quantification of the amount of complement factor H-related protein 4A in a sample.

name: blood group
definition: Any of the various types of human blood whose antigen characteristics determine compatibility in transfusion. While the ABO and Rhesus sytems are the most well known, there are in total about 300 different blood type antigens distributed across 34 different blood type systems.

name: ABO blood group
definition: The ABO system consists of A and B antigens and antibodies against these antigens.

name: blood group A
definition: ABO phenotype A, corresponding to the genotype AO or AA.

name: blood group B
definition: ABO phenotype B, corresponding to the genotype BO or BB.

name: blood group AB
definition: ABO phenotype AB, corresponding to the genotype AB.

name: blood group O
definition: ABO phenotype O, corresponding to the genotype OO.

name: serum lipopolysaccharide activity
definition: Quantification of lipopolysaccharide activity in serum.

name: response to tolvaptan
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of treatment with tolvaptan, an aquaretic drug that functions as a selective, competitive vasopressin receptor 2 (V2) antagonist.

name: nutritional supplement exposure measurement
definition: Quantification of some aspect of the consumption of dietary nutritional supplements.

name: mastiha supplement exposure measurement
definition: Quantification of some aspect of the consumption of mastiha, a natural nutritional supplement known to possess antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties.

name: obsolete_gene expression measurement
definition: Quantification of the expression of a gene in a cell, tissue or sample.

name: obsolete_tumor necrosis factor alpha gene expression measurement
synonyms: TNF superfamily, member 2 gene expression measurement
tumor necrosis factor gene expression measurement
definition: Quantification of the expression of the TNFA gene, which encodes tumor necrosis factor-alpha.

name: obsolete_interleukin-6 gene expression measurement
definition: Quantification of the expression of IL-6 gene, encoding interleukin-6.

name: obsolete_blood glutathione peroxidase measurement
definition: Quantification of glutathione peroxidase in a sample.

name: human polyomavirus 6 seropositivity
definition: The result of a measurement of circulating human polyomavirus 6-specific antibodies.

name: obsolete_anti-wu polyomavirus antibody measurement
definition: Quantification of one or more antibodies to the WU polyomavirus, typically in serum.

name: obsolete_anti-human polyomavirus 6 antibody measurement
definition: Quantification of one or more antibodies to the human polyomavirus 6, typically in serum.

name: response to stimulant therapy
synonyms: response to stimulant ADHD agent therapy
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulant such as used in the treatment of ADHD.

name: stimulant use measurement
definition: Quantification of some aspect of stimulant use, for instance in the treatment of ADHD.

name: cardiac troponin I change measurement
definition: Quantification of the change in cardiac troponin I in an individual over time, typically measured in blood.

name: Achilles tendon injury
definition: Any injury to the Achilles tendon, including bursitis, tendinitis, rupture or degeneration.

name: obsolete_glucocorticoid receptor gene expression measurement
definition: Quantification of glucocorticoid receptor gene expression.

name: response to recombinant tissue-plasminogen activator
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a recombinant tissue-plasminogen activator stimulus, a type of systemic thrombolytic agent.

name: time spent outdoors measurement
definition: Quantification of time an individual spends outside.

name: insulin use measurement
definition: Quantification of some aspect of the use of insulin.

name: family history of prostate cancer
definition: A reported family history of prostate cancer in one or more family members.

name: obsolete_bowel opening frequency
synonyms: average number of times bowels opened per day
definition: Number of times bowels opened per day.

name: PP interval
definition: An interval measured from the onset of the P wave in one PQRST wave complex to the onset of the P wave in the following PQRST wave complex.

name: appendectomy
definition: Procedure to remove the appendix.

name: obsolete_narrow occludable anterior chamber angle
definition: A narrow or occludable angle is when the angle of the eye is narrow or closed by the iris. Occludable anterior chamber angle is considered as a primary risk factor for primary angle closure glaucoma (PACG).

name: lymphocyte:monocyte ratio
definition: Quantification of the ratio between absolute lymphocyte count and absolute monocyte count.

name: peritoneal solute transfer rate
definition: Quantification of the rate at which small molecules cross the peritoneal membrane typically measured as the ratio of the concentration of creatinine in the dialysate at 4 hours of a dwell of dialysate solution to that in the plasma (4-hr D/P creatinine).

name: response to peritoneal dialysis
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a peritoneal dialysis.

name: complement factor H-related protein 4 measurement
definition: Quantification of the amount of complement factor H-related protein 4 in a sample.

name: complement factor H-like 1 protein measurement
definition: Quantification of complement factor H-like 1 protein in a sample.

name: response to cosmetics
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a cosmetic product stimulus.

name: obsolete_skin roughness measurement
definition: Quantification of some aspect of skin roughness such as frequency or severity.

name: primary dental caries
definition: The decay of any primary tooth, in which it becomes softened, discolored, and/or porous.

name: permanent dental caries
definition: The decay of any permanent tooth, in which it becomes softened, discolored, and/or porous.

name: spatial proteomics
definition: An assay that allows for visualization and quantification of proteins or associated antibodies used for evaluating in situ protein spatial distribution.

name: PhenoCycler-Fusion
definition: A spatial discovery system where whole-slide staining of tissues using pre-designed or custom antibody panels are imaged through automated fluidics (PhenoCycler) and high-speed image acquisition (PhenoImager).

name: PhenoCycler
definition: An automated fluidics system that uses oligonucleotide conjugated antibodies for tissue staining, followed by iterative cycles of applying fluorophore-conjugated reporter oligonucletides and gentle washing to generate multiplexed imaging data.

name: BD Rhapsody Whole Transcriptome Analysis
definition: A BD Biosciences-based technology that sequences mRNA from the 3' end in an unbiased manner.

name: BD Rhapsody Targeted mRNA
definition: A BD Biosciences-based technology that utilizes multiplex PCR to sequence mRNA from the 3' end of specific genes from a predetermined panel.

name: Abseq
definition: A method that uses DNA-tagged antibodies to quantify proteins in single cells.

name: ExSeq
definition: A spatial transcriptomics assay that involves physically expanding specimens with polymer- and hydrogel-based systems followed by in situ sequencing.

name: targeted ExSeq
definition: A spatial transcriptomics assay that involves physically expanding specimens with polymer- and hydrogel-based systems followed by targeted padlock probe hybridization, amplification, and in situ sequencing of padlock barcode.

name: untargeted ExSeq
definition: A spatial transcriptomics assay that involves physically expanding specimens with polymer- and hydrogel-based systems followed by reverse transcription, amplification, and in situ sequencing of untargeted RNA using FISSEQ.

name: transvaginal ultrasound-guided oocyte retrieval
synonyms: ultrasound-guided transvaginal needle aspiration of follicles
definition: A surgical technique used by medical professionals to extract mature eggs directly from an ovary with the guidance of ultrasound imaging.

name: TruDrop
definition: A droplet-based microfluidic library construction platform based on inDrop that incorporates dual-indexing to detect index-hopping and standard Illumina sequencing primers for high-throughput sequencing.

name: GEXSCOPE technology
definition: A microwell-based technology developed by Singleron to prepare mRNA from single cells or single nuclei and generate a next generation sequencing (NGS) library for high-throughput sequencing.

name: library preparation for spatial transcriptomics
definition: The library preparation step of a spatial transcriptomics assay.

name: oral rinse collection
definition: A saliva collection method where a solution such as a saline solution or other solution is used to rinse the mouth before collection of saliva.

name: ECCITE-seq
synonyms: expanded CRISPR-compatible cellular indexing of transcriptomes and epitopes by sequencing
definition: The collective capabilities of CITE-seq and Cell Hashing adapted for compatibility with the 5P / V(D)J single cell kit from 10x Genomics, to allow researchers to perform sample multiplexing, doublet detection and protein detection together with 5’ gene expression and V(D)J reconstruction.

name: PacBio Sequel II system
definition: The PacBio Sequel II system is a high-throughput, long-read sequencing machine developed by PacBio.

name: Smart-seq v4
definition: Library construction method using SMART (Switching Mechanism at the 5' end of the RNA Template) to generate high-quality cDNA from ultra-low amounts of total RNA or directly from multiple intact cells (<1,000 cells). Smart-seq v4 improves upon the Smart-seq2 method by incorporating both the novel use of locked nucleic acid (LNA) technology and an optimized template switching oligo.

name: pseudo-bulk aggregation of single-cell ATAC-seq data
definition: A processed matrix generation method that involves combining (binary or quantitative) single-cell ATAC seq data from multiple cells within the same biological sample and/or cell types, depending on the intended downstream values. Ideally, aggregation is done within predefined regions of the genome e.g., using called peaks or tiles across the genome. The aggregated profiles can then be used in the same manner as bulk ATAC-seq or DNase-seq data.

name: BGI MGISEQ-2000
definition: A next-generation sequencing (NGS) sequencer from Beijing Genomics Institute (BGI) based on DNA nanoball (DNB) and probe-anchor synthesis (cPAS) technology, which were also used in the previous version of the BGISEQ-500 device; however, the reagents for MGISEQ-2000 have been refined and the platform utilizes updated software.

name: ONT PromethION 2 Solo
definition: The ONT PromethION 2 Solo is a compact modular sequencing unit developed by Oxford Nanopore Technologies that can run up to two PromethION flow cells and connect to ONT GridION Mk1 devices.

name: Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome
definition: Birt-Hogg-Dube (BHD) syndrome is characterized by skin lesions, kidney tumors, and pulmonary cysts that may be associated with pneumothorax. It is a rare clinicopathologic condition named after the three Canadian physicians who reported the syndrome in 1977.

name: autosomal recessive Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy
definition: Autosomal recessive form of Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy.

name: lysosomal acid lipase deficiency
definition: Lysosomal acid lipase deficiency is a lipid storage disease that can result in 1) an early-onset severe form, Wolman disease, or 2) a less severe form, cholesteryl ester storage disease, of cholesteryl ester accumulation in the body (liver, spleen, macrophages). Wolman disease is characterized by neonatal abdominal distension, major or even massive hepatosplenomegaly and calcified adrenal glands, cholesteryl ester storage disease presents with microvesicular steatosis leading to hepatomegaly and hypercholesterolaemia with subsequent liver failure and accelerated atherosclerosis.

name: bleeding diathesis due to thromboxane synthesis deficiency
synonyms: bleeding diathesis due to thromboxane synthesis deficiency
definition: A rare, genetic, isolated constitutional thrombocytopenia disease characterized by impaired platelet aggregation resulting from a defect in thromboxane synthesis or signaling, manifesting with mild to moderate mucocutaneous, gastrointestinal or surgical bleeding (e.g. easy bruising, prolonged epistaxis, excessive bleeding after a tooth extraction).

name: familial mesial temporal lobe epilepsy with febrile seizures
definition: A rare, genetic, familial partial epilepsy disease characterized by simple partial seizures, complex partial seizures and/or secondarily generalized seizures, originating from the inner aspect of the temporal lobe, associated with an antecedant history of febrile seizures, ocurring in various members of a family. Hippocampal abnormalities (e.g. hippocampal sclerosis) may also be associated.

name: autosomal recessive optic atrophy
definition: A rare hereditary optic atrophy characterized by an early onset of bilateral optic nerve degeneration without other systemic features. Clinical manifestations include pallor of the optic disks, severe but slowly progressing visual impairment, and in some patients also paracentral scotoma, photophobia and dyschromatopsia.

name: autosomal dominant pure spastic paraplegia
synonyms: autosomal dominant pure hereditary spastic paraplegia
pure hereditary spastic paraplegia, autosomal dominant
definition: Autosomal dominant form of pure hereditary spastic paraplegia.

name: autosomal recessive complex spastic paraplegia
synonyms: autosomal recessive complex hereditary spastic paraplegia
complex hereditary spastic paraplegia, autosomal recessive
definition: Autosomal recessive form of complex hereditary spastic paraplegia.

name: gastroesophageal disease
definition: A class of gastroenterological diseases involving the stomch and or esophagus.

name: brain inflammatory disease
definition: An inflammatory disease involving a pathogenic inflammatory response in the brain.

name: syndromic anorectal malformation
definition: Anorectal malformations (ARMs) represent a complex group of congenital anomalies resulting from abnormal development of the hindgut, allantois and Mullerian duct resulting in complete or partial urorectal septal malformations. 50 % of cases are syndromic although many may have other associated anomalies.

name: autosomal dominant hereditary axonal motor and sensory neuropathy
definition: A form of axonal hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy with autosomal dominant inheritance.

name: autosomal recessive hereditary demyelinating motor and sensory neuropathy
definition: A form of demyelinating hereditary motor and sensory neuropathies (HMSN) with autosomal recessive inheritance. HMSNs are a group of inherited progressive neuropathies with markedly decreased nerve conduction velocity and chronic segmental demyelination in the peripheral nerve.

name: autosomal dominant hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy
synonyms: hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy, autosomal dominant
definition: A form of hereditary sensory autonomic neuropathy (HSAN) with autosomal dominant inheritance. HSANs are a group of rare peripheral neuropathies where neurons and/or axons are affected. The major feature of these conditions is the loss of large myelinated and unmyelinated fibers.

name: autosomal recessive hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy
synonyms: hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy, autosomal recessive
definition: A form of hereditary sensory autonomic neuropathy (HSAN) with autosomal recessive inheritance. HSANs are a group of rare peripheral neuropathies where neurons and/or axons are affected. The major feature of these conditions is the loss of large myelinated and unmyelinated fibers.

name: lateral facial cleft
definition: Lateral facial clefting (macrostomia) is a rare congenital malformation. It may occur either as an isolated phenomenon or in combination with other congenital anomalies.

name: familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy
definition: A rare familial cardiomyopathy characterized by the dilation of left ventricle and progressively impairing of systolic ventricular function, in the absence of abnormal loading conditions or coronary artery disease sufficient to cause global systolic impairment. The disease may cause heart failure or arrhythmia. The disease is isolated when no additional atypical cardiac or extracardiac manifestations are present.

name: benign familial mesial temporal lobe epilepsy
definition: Benign familial mesial temporal lobe epilepsy is a rare epilepsy characterized by seizures with viscerosensory or experential auras, onset in adolescence or early adulthood and good prognosis. It is defined as at least 24 months of seizure freedom with or without antiepileptic medication.

name: autosomal thrombocytopenia with normal platelets
definition: A form of hereditary thrombocytopenia with normal platelets.

name: congenital myopathy with cores
definition: Congenital myopathies represent a clinically and genetically heterogeneous group of early-onset neuromuscular diseases with characteristic, but not always specific, histopathological features, often presenting with stable and/or slowly progressive truncal and proximal weakness. The “core myopathies” collectively represent the most common form of congenital myopathies, and the name pathologically corresponds to histochemical appearance of focally reduced oxidative enzyme activity and myofibrillar changes on ultrastructural studies.

name: syndromic hypothyroidism
definition: Some forms of congenital hypothyroidism associated with defects in other organ systems are classified as syndromic hypothyroidism. These include Pendred syndrome, Bamforth-Lazarus syndrome and Kocher - Deber - Semilange syndrome.

name: acquired neutropenia
definition: An instance of neutropenia that is acquired during the lifetime of the individual.

name: primary immunodeficiency due to a defect in adaptive immunity
definition: Disorders of adaptive immunity (i.e., T-cell, B-cell or combined immunodeficiencies), a type of primary immunodeficiency disorder (PID), which constitute a heterogeneous group of disorders that result from defects in immune system development and/or function.

name: cerebellar malformation
definition: Cerebellar malformations are diverse congenital anomalies frequently associated with developmental disability.

name: ARX-related epileptic encephalopathy
definition: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-1 (DEE1) is a severe form of epilepsy characterized by frequent tonic seizures or spasms beginning in infancy. DEE1 is caused by mutation in the ARX gene.

name: cerebral malformation
definition: Disorders of the developing brain that constitute a wide variety of complex malformations that account for a significant fraction of childhood onset epilepsy, intellectual disability, and autism.

name: congenital myotonia
definition: Myotonia congenita (MC) is a genetic neuromuscular channelopathy which usually presents in early childhood resulting in a delay of skeletal muscle relaxation following contraction.

name: qualitative or quantitative defects of merosin
definition: Defects in merosin proteins, a group of laminins that share the alpha2 subunit encoded by the LAMA2 gene. Laminins are a family of high molecular weight glycoproteins that function as extracellular matrix components of the structural basement membrane.

name: qualitative or quantitative defects of calpain
definition: Defects in calpain protein, an intracellular protease that requires calcium for its catalytic activity.

name: qualitative or quantitative defects of myotubularin
definition: Defects in myotubularin, a protein required for muscle cell differentiation.

name: chronic acquired demyelinating polyneuropathy
definition: Chronic form of acquired peripheral neuropathy.

name: autosomal dominant proximal spinal muscular atrophy
synonyms: proximal spinal muscular atrophy, autosomal dominant
definition: A group of rare, genetic, motor neuron disease characterized by childhood or adult onset progressive, predominantly proximal, muscular weakness and wasting. Included diseases are Autosomal dominant adult-onset proximal spinal muscular atrophy, Lower motor neuron syndrome with late-adult onset, and Autosomal dominant childhood-onset proximal spinal muscular atrophy.

name: semilobar holoprosencephaly
definition: Semilobar holoprosencephaly is one of the classical forms of holoprosencephaly (HPE) in which the left and right frontal and parietal lobes are fused and the interhemispheric fissure is only present posteriorly.

name: primary congenital hypothyroidism
definition: Primary congenital hypothyroidism is a type of permanent congenital hypothyroidism, a permanent thyroid hormone deficiency that is present from birth.

name: isolated Klippel-Feil syndrome
definition: Klippel-Feil Syndrome is characterised by improper segmentation of cervical segments resulting in congenitally fused cervical vertebrae.

name: autosomal recessive lymphoproliferative disease
definition: A rare combined T and B cell immunodeficiency with a predisposition to lymphoproliferative syndrome. It is characterized by persistent symptomatic EBV-viremia and hypogammaglobulinemia variably presenting with fever, lymphadenopathy and systemic inflammatory conditions including hepatitis, pneumonia and sepsis. It may be associated with lymphoma, hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, and aplastic anemia.

name: progressive cerebello-cerebral atrophy
definition: A rare genetic neurological disorder characterized by postnatal onset of severe global developmental delay, profound mental retardation, progressive microcephaly, progressive spasticity evolving into spastic quadriplegia with joint contractures, generalized seizures, and irritability. Severe choreoathetosis and dysmorphic features are absent. Brain imaging shows progressive cerebellar atrophy followed by cerebral atrophy affecting both white and grey matter, but no pontine involvement.

name: autosomal dominant secondary polycythemia
definition: A rare, genetic, hematologic disease characterized by increased levels of serum hemoglobin, hematocrit and erythrocyte mass, associated with elevated or inappropriately normal erythropoietin serum levels, occurring in various members of a family and with autosomal dominant inheritance.

name: oligoastrocytic tumor
definition: Oligoastrocytomas (OA) are mixed gliomas with distinct oligodendroglial and astrocytic neoplastic components.

name: neuronal tumor
definition: Neuronal brain tumors are an uncommon group of central nervous system tumors that arise from cells with neuronal differentiation. These tumors may be purely neuronal in origin or have mixed neuronal and glial components, which comprise a subset of glioneuronal tumors.

name: Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy
synonyms: severe dystrophinopathy, Duchenne and Becker type
definition: Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophies (DMD and BMD) are neuromuscular diseases characterized by progressive muscle wasting and weakness due to degeneration of skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle.

name: hypomyelination neuropathy-arthrogryposis syndrome
definition: Hypomyelination neuropathy-arthrogryposis syndrome is a rare, genetic, limb malformation syndrome characterized by multiple congenital distal joint contractures (incl. talipes equinovarus and both proximal and distal interphalangeal joint contractures of the hands) and very severe motor paralysis at birth (i.e. lack of swallowing, autonomous respiratory function and deep tendon reflexes), leading to death within first 3 months of life. Fetal hypo- or akinesia, late-onset polyhydramnios and dramatically reduced, or absent, motor nerve conduction velocities (<10 m/s) are frequently associated. Nerve ultrastructural morphology shows severe abnormalities of the nodes of Ranvier and myelinated axons.

name: hereditary thrombocytopenia with normal platelets
definition: A rare, genetic, isolated constitutional thrombocytopenia disease characterized by decreased platelet counts, not associated with platelet morphology or function impairment, in multiple members of a family. Manifestations are variable, typically ranging from asymptomatic to mild bleeding diathesis (e.g. easy bruising, epistaxis, petechiae). Occasionally, a more severe bleeding tendency has been associated and a mild predisposition to infection and eczema has been reported.

name: midline cerebral malformation
definition: Cerebral midline anomalies are defects of anatomical relationships between the two hemispheres. They include holoprosencephalies, septal and commissural agenesis.

name: hereditary cardiac anomaly
definition: A group of inherited cardiac conditions (ICCs) that comprise a broad range of syndromes affecting the heart and major blood vessels, including cardiomyopathies, arrhythmias, aortopathies, familial hypercholesterolemia (FH), and congenital structural heart defects.

name: hereditary ATTR amyloidosis
definition: A rare genetic systemic disease characterized by adult onset, progressive sensorimotor and autonomic neuropathy and infiltrative cardiomyopathy. Neurological involvement usually starts with sensory loss in the extremities and progresses with motor neuropathy. Cardiomyopathy presents with rhythm abnormalities and heart failure. The disease also frequently manifests with a range of additional clinical signs and symptoms due to associated ocular, renal, central nervous system and gastrointestinal involvement.

name: sickle cell disease and related diseases
definition: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is an umbrella term that defines a group of inherited diseases (including sickle cell anaemia (SCA), HbSC and HbSβ-thalassaemia) characterized by mutations in the gene encoding the haemoglobin subunit β (HBB).

name: non-syndromic male infertility due to sperm motility disorder
synonyms: isolated male infertility due to sperm motility disorder
nonsyndromic male infertility due to sperm motility disorder
definition: Non-syndromic male infertility due to sperm motility disorder is a rare, genetic, non-syndromic male infertility disorder characterized by infertility due to sperm with defects in their cilia/flagella structure, leading to absent motility or reduced forward motility in fresh ejaculate. Reduced semen volume, oligospermia and an increased number of abnormally structured spermatozoa is often present.

name: septopreoptic holoprosencephaly
definition: Septopreoptic holoprosencephaly (HPE) is a very rare subtype of lobar HPE characterized by midline fusion limited to the septal and/or preoptic regions of the telencephalon without a significant frontal neocortical fusion.

name: inherited prion disease
definition: An instance of prion disease that is caused by an inherited modification of the individual's genome.

name: split hand or/and split foot malformation
definition: Split hand/foot malformation (SHFM) is a limb abnormality that is present at birth. It is characterized by absence of certain fingers and toes (ectrodactyly) that suggest a claw-like appearance and webbing of fingers and toes may also be present.

name: familial infantile gigantism
synonyms: infantile gigantism due to pituitary hyperplasia
definition: A rare, genetic pituitary disease characterized by infantile-onset, rapid and excessive acceleration of linear growth and body size due to mixed growth hormone (GH)- and prolactin-secreting adenomas and/or pituitary hyperplasia. Patients present with gigantism and may have associated acromegalic features (e.g. coarse facial features, frontal bossing, prognathism, increased interdental space) as well as marked enlargement of hands and feet, soft tissue swelling, increased appetite and acanthosis nigricans.

name: sodium channelopathy-related small fiber neuropathy
definition: A rare, genetic, peripheral neuropathy disorder due to gain-of-function mutations in voltage-gated sodium channels present in the small peripheral nerve fibers characterized by neuropathic pain of varying intensity (often beginning in the distal extermities and with a burning quality) associated with autonomic dysfunction (e.g. orthostatic dizziness, palpitations, dry eyes and mouth), abnormal quantitative sensory testing, and reduction in intraepidermal nerve ﬁber density. Large fiber functions (i.e. normal strength, tendon reflexes, and vibration sense) and nerve conduction studies are typically normal.

name: pure or complex autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia
synonyms: Pure or complicated autosomal recessive spastic paraplegia
definition: A form of hereditary spastic paraplegia with autosomal recessive inheritence.

name: deafness-onychodystrophy syndrome
definition: Deafness-onychodystrophy syndrome is a group of rare, genetic, developmental defect during embryogenesis disorders characterized by the association of sensorineural deafness and onychodystrophy (e.g. absent/hypoplastic finger and toenails), as well as brachydactyly and finger-like thumbs. Additional features present in one of the diseases comprising this group include osteodystrophy, intellectual disability, seizures, developmental delay, and distinctive facies.

name: microcephalic primordial dwarfism
definition: Primordial dwarfism with microcephaly.

name: isolated scaphocephaly
definition: Isolated scaphocephaly is a form of nonsyndromic craniosynostosis characterized by premature fusion of the sagittal suture.

name: isolated plagiocephaly
definition: isolated plagiocephaly is a form of non-syndromic unicoronal synostosis.

name: isolated brachycephaly
definition: Isolated brachycephaly is a relatively frequent nonsyndromic craniosynostosis consisting of premature fusion of both coronal sutures leading to skull deformity with a broad flat forehead and palpable coronal ridges.

name: congenital myasthenic syndromes with glycosylation defect
definition: Congenital myasthenic syndrome with glycosylation defect is a group of genetic disorders of impaired neuromuscular transmission at the motor endplate characterized by fatigable muscle weakness with a defect in glycosylation.

name: hereditary intestinal polyposis
definition: An inherited form of intestinal polyps that include familial adenomatous polyposis and juvenile polyposis syndrome.

name: primary short bowel syndrome
definition: Short bowel syndrome is a complex disease that occurs due to the physical loss or the loss of function of a portion of the small and/or large intestine. Consequently, individuals with short bowel syndrome often have a reduced ability to absorb nutrients such as fats, carbohydrates (sugars) vitamins, minerals, trace elements and fluids (malabsorption).

name: homozygous 2p21 microdeletion syndrome
definition: Homozygous deletion of chromosome 2p21, containing two closely located genes, SLC3A1, and PREPL, has been linked to the hypotonia–cystinuria syndrome. Symptoms include generalized hypotonia at birth, failure to thrive, cystinuria, and growth retardation.

name: fetal anticonvulsant syndrome
definition: Syndromes associated with congenital malformations and cognitive disorders in children whose mothers took antiepileptic drugs in pregnancy.

name: congenital muscular dystrophy with cerebellar involvement
definition: A rare, congenital muscular dystrophy due to dystroglycanopathy characterized by proximal muscle weakness with a tendency for muscle hypertrophy and pseudohypertrophy, variable cognitive impairment, microcephaly, cerebellar hypoplasia with or without cysts, and other structural brain anomalies.

name: congenital muscular dystrophy without intellectual disability
synonyms: congenital muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy without intellectual disability
definition: A rare, genetic, congenital muscular dystrophy due to dystroglycanopathy characterized by a wide phenotypic spectrum which includes hypotonia and muscular weakness present at birth or early infancy, delayed or arrested motor development, and normal intellectual abilities with normal (or only mild abnormalities) neuroimaging studies. Feeding difficulties, joint and spinal deformities, and respiratory insufficiency may be associated. Decreased alpha-dystroglycan on immunohistochemical muscle staining and elevated serum creatine kinase are observed.

name: primary qualitative or quantitative defects of alpha-dystroglycan
definition: Defects in the alpha unit of the dystroglycan protein, a high-affinity receptor for several extracellular matrix components.

name: hereditary isolated aplastic anemia
definition: Hereditary isolated aplastic anemia is a rare, genetic, constitutional aplastic anemia disorder characterized by severe peripheral blood pancytopenia and bone marrow hypoplasia in multiple individuals of a family, in the absence of any somatic symptoms.

name: male infertility with azoospermia or oligozoospermia due to single gene mutation
definition: Male infertility with azoospermia or oligospermia due to single gene mutation is a rare, genetic male infertility due to sperm disorder characterized by the absence of a measurable amount of spermatozoa in the ejaculate (azoospermia), or a number of sperm in the ejaculate inferior to 15 million/mL (oligozoospermia), resulting from a mutation in a single gene known to cause azoo- or oligo-spermia. Sperm morphology may be normal.

name: X-linked distal hereditary motor neuropathy
definition: X-linked form of distal hereditary motor neuropathy.

name: intellectual disability-expressive aphasia-facial dysmorphism syndrome
synonyms: intellectual disability-loss of expressive language-facial dysmorphism syndrome
definition: A rare genetic syndromic intellectual disability characterized by moderate to severe intellectual deficiency, language deficit (completely absent or significantly impaired speech), and distinctive facial dysmorphism (long face, straight eyebrows, and, less frequently, low-set ears and café-au-lait spots).

name: microcephalic primordial dwarfism-insulin resistance syndrome
definition: A rare genetic disease characterized by severe pre- and postnatal growth failure with short stature and microcephaly, facial dysmorphism (including a small jaw and prominent midface), severe insulin resistance, fatty liver, and hypertriglyceridemia developing in childhood, and primary gonadal failure. Mild global learning difficulties and acanthosis nigricans have also been reported.

name: congenital nemaline myopathy
definition: A rare genetic muscle disorder defined by muscle weakness and the presence of fine, thread-like or rod-like structures called “nemaline bodies”, when muscle biopsies are viewed under the microscope.

name: familial patent arterial duct
definition: Familial patent arterial duct is a rare, genetic, non-syndromic, congenital anomaly of the great arteries characterized by the presence of an isolated patent arterial duct (PDA) (i.e. failure of closure of ductus arteriosis after birth) in several members of the same family.

name: axonal hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy
definition: A form of hereditary motor and sensory neuropathies, a group of slowly progressive inherited disorders affecting motor and sensory peripheral nerves.

name: type 1 interferonopathy
definition: Conditions in which increased type 1 interferon signaling leads to autoimmune and neurological disorders. These disorders are caused by variants in genes involved in nucleic acid metabolism, sensing, and the innate immune response.

name: COL4A1 or COL4A2-related cerebral small vessel disease
definition: COL4A1 and COL4A2 genes encode the alpha1 and the alpha2 chains of type IV collagen, a key component of basement membranes. Mutations located in the coding sequence of COL4A1/COL4A2 genes are responsible for an autosomal dominant (AD) cerebral angiopathy that manifest in either adults, children or fetuses.

name: HTRA1-related cerebral small vessel disease
definition: A rare genetic cerebral small vessel disease characterized by subcortical ischemic events associated with cognitive decline and gait disturbance with an age of onset typically in the sixth or seventh decade of life. Imaging reveals white matter hyperintensities, status cribrosus, lacunar infarcts, and sometimes microbleeds. Extra-neurological manifestations are absent.

name: congenital cornea plana
definition: A rare developmental defect of the eye characterized by usually bilateral absence of the normal protrusion of the cornea from the sclera, the corneal curvature being the same as that of the adjacent sclera. Most patients develop hyperopia, hazy corneal limbus, and arcus lipoides at an early age. The condition may present as an autosomal dominant or an autosomal recessive form, with the latter showing more severe signs and symptoms (such as a round and opaque thickening located centrally in the cornea) and more frequent association with other ocular anomalies.

name: isolated anorectal malformation
definition: A wide spectrum of malformations involving the distal anus and rectum as well as the urinary and genital tracts, which can affect boys and girls.

name: vascular anomaly
definition: Vascular anomalies are abnormalities or disorders of the vascular system, either in veins or arteries. Vascular anomalies are classified as either a vascular tumor or a vascular malformation.

name: intractable diarrhea of infancy
definition: Prolonged diarrhea of infants younger than 3 months old that persists longer than 2 weeks with negative stool cultures.

name: familial isolated restrictive cardiomyopathy
definition: Adults with familial restrictive cardiomyopathy typically first develop shortness of breath, fatigue, and a reduced ability to exercise. Some individuals have an irregular heart beat (arrhythmia) and may also experience a sensation of fluttering or pounding in the chest (palpitations) and dizziness.

name: trichorhinophalangeal syndrome type I or III
definition: Trichorhinophalangeal syndrome type I and III are extremely rare inherited multisystem disorders.

name: inborn disorder of gamma-aminobutyric acid metabolism
synonyms: inborn error of gamma-aminobutyric acid metabolic process
inborn gamma-aminobutyric acid metabolic process disorder
rare inborn error of gamma-aminobutyric acid metabolic process
definition: GABA-T deficiency is associated with severe neonatal/early infantile epileptic encephalopathy and growth acceleration.

name: myoclonic epilepsy of infancy
definition: Myoclonic epilepsy of infancy is a rare self-limited epileptic syndrome characterized by brief myoclonic seizures in previously healthy and developmentally normal children in the first three years of life.
